units.text: INT. COUNTY RECORDS BASEMENT - DAY
Steel shelving in grey rows.
A single folding table has been set under a humming fluorescent tube.
Dust hangs in the light like flour.
JUDGE ILSA BRANDVOLD, 60s, reading glasses on a chain, sits at the head of the table with a legal pad.
Across from her, ATTORNEY RAJESH PILLAY, 40s, rumpled suit, pulls a banker's box toward him and lifts the lid.

At the far end, CLERK FERGUS MBEKI, 20s, bow tie, sorts folders into piles while ATTORNEY LOUISE ARCENEAUX, 50s, crisp navy blazer, pretends not to watch the box and instead straightens her pen, then her water glass, then her notes, then glances at Pillay, who pays her no mind and hums as he unfolds a brittle deed.
We are on the record. Counsel, you said there was a discrepancy in the plat.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: There is a lot line, Your Honor, that appears on the 1962 survey and not on the 1974 survey.
units.name: PILLAY

units.text: Which is irrelevant, as the 1974 survey supersedes.
units.name: ARCENEAUX

units.text: Unless the 1974 survey was never recorded.
units.name: PILLAY

units.text: Mbeki stops sorting.
He checks a ledger, runs a finger down a column, then looks up with the slow expression of a man who has found something unwelcome.
It was recorded, Judge. In the wrong book.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: The wrong book.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Deed book instead of plat book. Somebody misfiled it fifty years ago.
units.name: MBEKI

units.text: Arceneaux sets down her pen.

Pillay finally smiles, folds the deed back along its crease, and slides it across the table toward the judge while Brandvold removes her glasses, polishes them on her sleeve, replaces them, and reads, and Mbeki hovers behind her with the ledger open, and Arceneaux leans to see.
That's a clerical error. It doesn't alter the legal effect.
units.name: ARCENEAUX

units.text: It alters the date.
units.name: PILLAY

units.text: Mr. Mbeki, bring me the plat book.
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: He crosses the room, hauls down a canvas-bound volume, wipes it with his cuff, and sets it before her.
She turns pages, slowly, one at a time.
We will be here a while. Would anyone like coffee?
units.name: BRANDVOLD

units.text: Please.
units.name: ARCENEAUX

units.text: Black, thanks.
units.name: PILLAY

units.text: Mbeki nods and heads for the stairs, already counting cups.
